source_reachability:
All statuses observed by me on 2026-09-16 with curl -A "Mokaair-editorial".

THE 4 RECORDED SOURCES:
1. https://openai.com/news/rss.xml — HTTP 200, text/xml, 726,611 bytes. Real RSS (channel title "OpenAI News"), 1,195 <item>, newest pubDate Wed, 16 Sep 2026 16:00:00 GMT, oldest Fri, 11 Dec 2015. Live feed, not a rejection page.
2. https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=&entityName=OpenAI — HTTP 200, application/json, 32,681 bytes, real EDGAR FTS response, hits.total.value = 46.
3. https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title15/html/USCODE-2023-title15-chap2A-subchapI-sec77f.htm — HTTP 200, text/html, 24,007 bytes, US Code 2023 edition, "Sec. 77f - Registration of securities". Correct document.
4. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/05/21/2026-10222.txt — HTTP 200, text/plain, 657,682 bytes, full text of 91 FR 30086. This URL is the raw_text_url field the FR API returns, so it is not a constructed guess.

OTHER URLS THE RESEARCHER ATTACHED TO FACTS:
https://openai.com/sitemap.xml/company/ — HTTP 200, application/xml, 1,238,668 bytes, 261 <url>. Listed in https://openai.com/sitemap.xml (HTTP 200), so not guessed.
https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=&entityName=OpenAI&forms=DRS — HTTP 200, total 0 (same for S-1, F-1, DRS/A, S-1/A, 8-A12B, 424B4).
https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22OpenAI%22&forms=DRS — HTTP 200, total 121.
https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=&entityName=OpenAI&dateRange=custom&startdt=2026-06-01&enddt=2026-09-16 — HTTP 200, total 2.
https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001877240.json — HTTP 200, 1,568 bytes.
https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-10222.json — HTTP 200, 42,157 bytes.
https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-14/title-17.xml?part=239&section=239.11 — HTTP 200 with --compressed; HTTP 406 without a compression Accept-Encoding header (researcher's note confirmed).
https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title15-section77f&num=0&edition=prelim — HTTP 200, 175,241 bytes.
https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json?conditions[term]=OpenAI&conditions[publication_date][gte]=2026-01-01&per_page=20&order=newest — HTTP 200, count=2.
https://www.sec.gov/news/pressreleases.rss — HTTP 200, application/rss+xml, 18,402 bytes, real feed with 25 items (researcher's discovery confirmed).

BLOCKS CONFIRMED (not reachable, correctly excluded):
https://openai.com/index/openai-submits-confidential-s-1 — HTTP 403, server: cloudflare, cf-mitigated: challenge, body is the "Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue" challenge page. Same 403 for the trailing-slash, /zh-Hant/ and /ja-JP/ variants.
https://www.sec.gov/about/divisions-offices/division-corporation-finance/voluntary-submission-draft-registration-statements-faqs — HTTP 403.
https://www.sec.gov/about/divisions-offices/division-corporation-finance/draft-registration-statement-processing-procedures-expanded — HTTP 403.
https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/21/2026-10222/enhancement-of-emerging-growth-company-accommodations-and-simplification-of-filer-status-for — HTTP 302 to https://unblock.federalregister.gov/.

NEW AND REACHABLE (better first-party route, researcher missed it):
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-05-21/pdf/2026-10222.pdf — HTTP 200. GPO's own copy of the same Federal Register document.
https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002021728.json — HTTP 200. The correct source for the Cerebras control-group facts.

refuted.fact: F11: the 46 EDGAR filings under entityName=OpenAI belong to 30 filers
refuted.why: It is 41 distinct filers, not 30. efts.sec.gov returns at most 30 buckets in its entity_filter aggregation; the researcher read a truncated aggregation as a complete list. Expanding all 46 hits' display_names gives 41 distinct filers (one filing, 2024-03-22, has two co-filers: MAV OpenAI Fund I and QP-MAV OpenAI Fund I). Filers invisible in the aggregation include OpenAI Startup Fund II, L.P., SPV I, SPV V, SPV VI, OurCrowd (Investment in G-new OpenAI) L.P., OpenAI Tender Fund I Sep 2025, OpenAI-01 a Series of OpenAI Opp Fund LLC, OpenAI-s a Series of GatePass Ventures I LLC, Starbridge OpenAI 1 Jul 2025 and VM OpenAI 1 a Series of PCXS LLC. The rest of F11 (all third-party VC funds/SPVs, no OpenAI entity itself) I verified and it holds.

refuted.fact: F30: the 25 items in the SEC press-release RSS cover only 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-16
refuted.why: They cover 2026-07-08 to 2026-09-16 - over two months, not two weeks. The oldest item is Wed, 08 Jul 2026 13:54:26 -0400 'SEC to Host Virtual Roundtable on Modernizing IPOs and Expanding Access to Public Markets'. The researcher's conclusion (the window excludes June, so it cannot prove there was no June press release) still stands, but the stated range is wrong and must not be copied into the article. I did confirm the feed body contains no 'OpenAI' and no 'draft registration'.

refuted.fact: editorial_brief (derived from F10): 'all 46 filings are Form D'
refuted.why: 40 of the 46 have file_type D and 6 have file_type D/A (amendments to a Form D). The form_filter aggregation groups by root form, which is why it displays D:46. F10's literal description of the aggregation is accurate, but the editorial_brief's restatement is not. Correct phrasing: 'all 46 are Form D or amendments to it (40 Form D, 6 Form D/A)'.

unsupported.fact: F4: the feed had 1,194 <item> when fetched on 2026-09-16
unsupported.why: I fetched the same feed at 16:12 UTC on 2026-09-16 and counted 1,195 <item>. This is same-day drift on a live feed rather than a transcription error, but it is exactly the kind of ever-increasing number the BRIEF forbids putting in front of readers. It must not appear in the article, and the research note should be rewritten as 'over 1,100 items, newest pubDate equal to the check date'. The other two criteria in F4 (newest item 2026-09-16, feed is live) I confirmed.

unsupported.fact: F15 (second half): Cerebras Systems Inc.'s 2026-05-04 S-1/A, file number 333-295145
unsupported.why: It is attached to https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22OpenAI%22&forms=DRS, a query restricted to forms=DRS whose response contains only DRS and DRS/A filings and carries no file-number field at all. The fact cannot be traced to the one URL cited, so under the BRIEF it is unsupported. I independently verified the fact itself at https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002021728.json (HTTP 200) - see additional_findings. F15's first half (Cerebras Systems Inc., CIK 0002021728, DRS/A dated 2026-03-31, present in that query) is confirmed.

unsupported.fact: F18 (short titles only): calling Pub. L. 112-106 the 'JOBS Act' and Pub. L. 114-94 the 'FAST Act'
unsupported.why: The govinfo §77f page contains none of the strings JOBS, FAST, Jumpstart or Fixing America - I searched the full text. It gives only 'Pub. L. 112-106, title I, §106(a), Apr. 5, 2012, 126 Stat. 312' and 'Pub. L. 114-94, div. G, title LXXI, §§71001, 71002, Dec. 4, 2015', plus the amendment note substituting '15 days' for '21 days', all of which I confirmed verbatim. The two short titles must be re-attributed to 91 FR 30086, which does state Public Law 112-106 is the JOBS Act and Public Law 114-94 is the Fixing America's Surface Transportation ('FAST') Act.

unsupported.fact: Provenance not recorded for the govinfo USCODE URL, the uscode.house.gov granuleid URL, and Federal Register document number 2026-10222
unsupported.why: All three are identifiers that can be constructed from a pattern, and the research record does not say which official search produced them. I fetched all three and they resolve to exactly the claimed documents (§77f, §77f prelim, 91 FR 30086), so this is not fabrication - but under the BRIEF's rule that a correct guess is still a guess, the research record should state how they were found. By contrast the researcher did document the provenance of https://openai.com/sitemap.xml/company/ and the Federal Register raw_text_url, and I verified both: the former is listed in the sitemapindex at https://openai.com/sitemap.xml, the latter is the raw_text_url field the API returns.

additional_findings: Better first-party route the researcher missed: the same Federal Register document is readable on GPO's own site at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-05-21/pdf/2026-10222.pdf (HTTP 200, and it is the pdf_url the FR API returns, not a guess), while federalregister.gov's human-readable HTML page 302s to unblock.federalregister.gov. Consider putting the govinfo URL in sources instead of, or alongside, the federalregister raw text.

Date distinction the research record omits: the proposed rule was adopted by the Commission on 2026-05-19 ('By the Commission. Dated: May 19, 2026. Vanessa A. Countryman, Secretary.') and published in the Federal Register on 2026-05-21. The article must not say the SEC proposed it on May 21.

The correct source for the Cerebras control group is https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002021728.json (HTTP 200), and its full track is more useful than what was recorded: DRS 2025-12-22 and DRS/A 2026-03-31 (both under file number 377-08857), then S-1 2026-04-17, S-1/A 2026-05-04, S-1/A 2026-05-11, 8-A12B 2026-05-11 (001-43284) and 424B4 2026-05-14 (the S-1 series all under 333-295145); tickers ['CBRS'], exchanges ['Nasdaq']. The change of file-number prefix from 377- while confidential to 333- once publicly filed illustrates the confidential-to-public transition far better than 'other companies' DRS are findable'.

Methodological trap worth writing into the research record for later batches: efts.sec.gov returns at most 30 entity_filter buckets, sic_filter was an empty array for this query, and form_filter groups by root form so D/A collapses into D. Any 'how many filers' or 'all of them are form X' conclusion must be computed by expanding the hits, never read off the aggregation.

A sentence of 15 U.S.C. §77f(e)(1) the researcher did not record and that the article could use: an issuer that was an emerging growth company when it submitted a confidential registration statement but ceases to be one afterwards continues to be treated as an EGC for this subsection through the earlier of consummating its IPO or the end of the one-year period after it ceases to qualify. This supports the article's stance of not classifying OpenAI, because EGC status is judged as of the submission.

The SEC press-release feed the researcher actually fetched contains one same-period, on-topic official item that was not noted: 2026-07-08 'SEC to Host Virtual Roundtable on Modernizing IPOs and Expanding Access to Public Markets'. It is not about OpenAI, but it is the only first-party lead in that feed if the article wants to mention SEC activity on IPO process in 2026.

Sourcing compliance is clean: none of the 30 facts is attributed to a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet. Everything sits on openai.com, efts.sec.gov, data.sec.gov, govinfo.gov, uscode.house.gov, federalregister.gov, ecfr.gov or sec.gov official channels. Vendor-claim marking is correct (F3 carries is_vendor_claim). F6 and F7 are marked as vendor claims although they are objective observations of the feed - over-cautious but harmless.

I confirmed that using the RSS URL in sources is forced rather than lazy: the article page and its zh-Hant and ja-JP variants all return HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge body (cf-mitigated: challenge). The BRIEF's rule that sources carry the article URL and not the feed URL genuinely cannot be met here; the researcher flagged the conflict for editorial judgement, which is the right handling.
The OpenAI item's title and description are pure ASCII - I checked every character. No U+2011 or non-breaking-space traps, so 'Confidential submission of draft S-1 to the SEC' can be typed as-is.

not_said (12 entries) and unverified_or_excluded (10 entries) are substantive and I found no material gap in them: they cover the submission date, the legal entity, exchange, ticker, valuation, timing, EGC classification and draft S-1 contents, and they correctly warn that the Form D VC/SPV list is easily misread as 'OpenAI itself has SEC filings'.

I re-ran the no-follow-up check with a much wider keyword set (S-1, SEC, prospectus, road show, public markets, restructur, PBC, Foundation, valuation, investor, equity, capital) across every 2026 item in the feed. The 2026-06-08 item is the only hit on S-1, and there is no later OpenAI announcement about the submission, a listing or a public filing. F5's conclusion holds on the stronger test.
